rows.feature: A Finance tab on the project with seven sub-tabs
rows.what: The project page has a Finance tab with Overview · Contract/VO · Invoices · POs · Expenses · Bills · Receipts sub-tabs, each with a one-line description.
rows.v2: Project › Money (one page: Needs you · To collect / To pay / Profit tiles · Billing · Costs)
rows.how: One Money tab replaces the seven sub-tabs. Money in is the Billing list (the payment stages, then “Outside the stages”, then “Changes to the contract” for variation orders); Owners and Admins can switch Billing to Invoices · Payments · Credit notes views. Money out is the Costs list.

rows.feature: The count on the Finance tab
rows.what: “Finance (n)” counts the project’s invoices that are not paid or void, drafts included.
rows.v2: Project › tab strip › Money (n)
rows.how: The count is what waits on the person looking (the Money rows of Needs you: approvals, payments to confirm, ready invoices, overdue ones…), not every unpaid invoice.

rows.feature: Opening a sub-tab or one invoice from a link
rows.what: The address carries ?tab=finance&sub=… and &focus=<invoice> opens that invoice’s row, scrolled to and flashed.
rows.v2: Project › Money ?open=<record>&do=<step>
rows.how: `/projects/{id}/money?open=<invoice|payment|credit note|VO|PO…>` lights the row and opens its side panel; `&do=remind|record|confirm|approve|sendback` opens that step; `&send=1` opens Send. Anchors #billing · #costs · #changes.

rows.feature: Ways into the money from elsewhere
rows.what: The Overview’s Key Files, every finance issue, Studio Finance’s “View Project” and a Pipeline PO card link to the project’s Finance tab.
rows.v1: Project › Overview · Finance › Operations · Finance › Pipeline
rows.v2: Overview › Money card · Needs you rows · the bell · Activity · ⌘K (invoice numbers) · Company › Finance › To do · Schedule › milestone panel › Invoices
rows.how: More doors, all landing on the record with ?open=; the Schedule’s milestone panel lists its stage’s invoices.

rows.feature: Who sees a project’s money
rows.what: Anyone who can open the project sees the whole Finance tab (contract, costs, profit); the finance permissions in the role editor are never checked, and the tab hides only behind a platform switch.
rows.v2: Project › Money (or a lock: “Money is the project’s team’s”)
rows.how: Only the project’s team, their Manager, Owners and Admins see Money; cost, profit and margin go to Owners and Admins only. Every money action checks this on the server.

rows.feature: Who may approve, void, reverse and override
rows.what: Browser-side role tags decide who sees Approve, Re-sync, Override schedule and so on (Owner / Admin / Accounting, with “accountant” vs “accounting” mismatches); many server routes check no role.
rows.v2: Project › Money (each step’s refusal is said in its menu row)
rows.how: One rule set, checked on the server: the team prepares, sends (or submits) invoices and records payments; Owners and Admins approve invoices, void, reverse payments, mark a VO approved and issue credit notes; the chosen confirmer (or an Owner / Admin) confirms a client’s payment.

rows.feature: An Accounting role for money
rows.what: Finance permissions and some screens treat an “accounting” member as an approver of invoices, POs and payment verification.

rows.feature: The Income menu and the Record Payment button
rows.what: “Income ▾” offers Raise an invoice and Raise a variation order; a separate Record Payment button opens a payment drawer.
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Bill {client} (Variation order · Variation order from a contractor’s quote · One-off invoice · Record an invoice made elsewhere)
rows.how: No “Raise an invoice”: each stage’s invoice already exists as a Draft. Record a payment sits on each sent invoice (its row’s Next step, its panel, its page, Needs you).

rows.feature: Billing locked while the project is a Draft
rows.what: On a Draft project, invoices, VOs and POs are disabled (or refused with a toast); the server refuses invoices.

rows.feature: AI Insights on the project’s money
rows.what: An “AI Insights” button sends the project’s invoices, POs, VOs and expenses to an AI for 3–5 insights per sub-tab (canned sample figures with no AI key).
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you (Owners and Admins: insight rows)
rows.how: Rules over the real records, no AI and no button: costs above the contract, margin At risk / Tight, a PO over the client’s price, paid out more than collected, VOs over 10% — shown as Needs you rows to Owners and Admins, each opening its record.

rows.feature: Links to Studio Finance from each sub-tab
rows.what: “View in Studio Finance ↗” opens Finance › Operations filtered to this project (Owner / Admin / Accounting only).
rows.v2: Company › Finance › To do (each row opens the project’s Money)
rows.how: Finance is a Company section; its To do lists money-in steps across projects (to approve, to collect, to confirm, ready to send). No link from Money to it.

rows.feature: Contract value = signed quote + approved client VOs
rows.what: The contract is the latest client-signed quote (else an approved primary quote, else the budget field) plus approved client VOs, never below zero.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Overview · Overview › Financial Summary
rows.v2: Project › Money (To collect’s hover) · Overview › Money card › Contract value
rows.how: Base = the signed quote, else the Won quote, else a direct project’s agreed value (set on the Overview); 1.0’s budget field and “approved primary quote” fallbacks are gone. One calculation feeds every surface.

rows.feature: GST split out of every slice
rows.what: A quote’s total includes GST; each payment slice splits GST out at the base quote’s rate (or the lead’s GST switch); nothing adds GST on top.
rows.v2: Project › Money (each stage’s “GST S$x inside”)

rows.feature: Where the contract value comes from, said on the card
rows.what: The Financial Summary says “From signed quote · n line items · includes +S$x VOs” or “From project budget · no signed quote yet”.
rows.v2: Overview › Money card (“From the signed quote” / “Agreed value”) · Money › To collect hover

rows.feature: The payment schedule is the milestones that carry a %
rows.what: A project’s schedule is the timeline milestones with a payment percentage; it is seeded from the quote’s payment schedule at creation.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing (the stages) · Schedule › milestone panel › “A payment falls due here”
rows.how: The stages are the signed quote’s Payment Schedule rows (a direct project’s chosen split). A milestone can be tied to a stage, due when it starts or when it is done; the stage then reads Ready to send.

rows.feature: Payment schedule templates
rows.what: Accounts Setup › Payment Schedules: a name, a Default tick, stages with name, % and a trigger (Contract Signed · Work Started · Milestone Completed · Project Completed · Custom Date), drag to reorder, must total 100%; new ones start 10/40/40/10.
rows.v2: Company › Templates › Payment schedules
rows.how: Each stage has a name, a description and a share %; one studio default; presets 10/30/30/30 · 20/40/40 · 30/70 · 50/50. No trigger list (a quote row is due on approval, on an estimated or a fixed date) and no drag.

rows.feature: A project’s own split when there is no system quote
rows.what: A project with no signed quote bills against its budget; its milestones carry their own %.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Pick the payment split / Change the split
rows.how: A direct project picks a split (from a template or its own rows, each tied to a milestone); it can change until a stage invoice is sent, with Undo.

rows.feature: Change a milestone’s share on a running project
rows.what: The Payment Structure dialog edits one milestone’s %, blocks over 100%; the schedule locks once set, an Owner / Admin can override (logged), and an invoiced milestone stays locked.
rows.v1: Project › Management › Gantt › milestone › Payment Structure
rows.how: The agreed shares never move on a quote-based project; a Draft’s amount can change with a reason instead.

rows.feature: Commission triggered by a milestone
rows.what: Each payment milestone has a “Trigger commission” switch: commission accrues when that milestone is finalised.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Commission · Company › Finance › Commission
rows.how: Commission is worked out from the payments that count (or the profit, or a fixed amount) by the studio’s rules; no per-milestone switch.

rows.feature: Shares must total 100% before the schedule goes out
rows.what: Publishing the timeline is blocked while payment percentages do not add up to 100 (“…x% unallocated”).
rows.v2: Quote editor › Send (readiness) · Money › Payment split dialog
rows.how: Checked where the split is set: the quote’s readiness refuses a Payment Schedule that is not 100%, and a direct project’s split refuses one that is not.

rows.feature: Fixed-amount (“fee first”) stage
rows.what: Behind a studio switch (off everywhere), a fixed stage such as “Design fees S$3,000” can open the schedule before the % stages, through quotes, invoices and the rebalance.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Invoices › “May open with a fixed fee” · Money › Payment split
rows.how: Built for a direct project’s split only (the first stage may be a fixed amount). A quote’s Payment Schedule rows are percentages, so a quote-based project cannot open with a fixed fee.

rows.feature: One invoice per payment stage
rows.what: A second invoice for the same milestone returns the existing one (“Already invoiced — opening INV-…”); an invoice is matched to its milestone by key, id or name.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing (one row per stage)

rows.feature: What each stage bills, catch-up included
rows.what: One allocation decides what an unbilled milestone bills: the contract less locked invoices, shared by %; the picker shows “(incl. catch-up)” when it differs from the nominal share.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Overview timeline · milestone picker
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing (Amount) · the invoice paper

rows.feature: Re-size the unsent drafts when the contract moves (rebalance)
rows.what: After a VO is approved or revised, an invoice is inserted, or on demand, the unsent drafts are re-sized by their %; sent and paid invoices never change.
rows.v2: Project › Money (a snackbar sentence with Undo)

rows.feature: “Re-sync to contract” on demand
rows.what: A Re-sync button (finance roles) re-sizes the drafts and toasts the outcome or the reason nothing changed.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you › “The unsent invoices don’t add up…” › Even them out
rows.how: No standing button: the row appears only when the drafts are out of step, for the team, Owners and Admins, with Undo.

rows.feature: A supplement invoice when no draft is left
rows.what: When no unsent draft can carry new contract money, the rebalance creates a draft “Supplement — contract adjustment”.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you › “VO-n is approved with no unsent invoice to carry it” › Bill VO-n
rows.how: The approved order is billed on its own Draft (its own total) instead of a generic supplement.

rows.feature: A draft credit note when the contract falls below what is billed
rows.what: If billed exceeds the new contract, the rebalance writes an invisible draft credit note (“review it under Credit Notes”, a place that does not exist).
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you › “S$x billed above the contract” › Issue a credit note
rows.how: Nothing hidden is written: the excess shows as a row and the credit note dialog opens filled in.

rows.feature: Raise an invoice from a milestone picker
rows.what: The invoice drawer lists each payment milestone with its state and amount (Bill · Complete & Invoice… · Open), plus an ad-hoc row; a bulk “Generate Invoices” dialog also exists, unreachable.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Income › Raise an invoice
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing
rows.how: Every stage has its Draft from the project’s start; the Billing row shows its milestone, amount, state (Draft · Ready to send) and Next step, so there is nothing to pick.

rows.feature: Complete the milestone and bill it in one flow
rows.what: “Complete & bill…” marks the milestone done (or submits it for approval) then opens the invoice; completing a milestone on the Gantt drafts its invoice and offers “Send to homeowner”.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Overview timeline · Gantt › Complete Milestone
rows.v2: Schedule › Mark done sheet › “Send the {stage} invoice” · Money › Needs you › Send the {stage} invoice · the bell (“ready to send”)
rows.how: Done and the invoice are ticks on one sheet; the invoice is the allocation’s amount, never the nominal slice (1.0’s Gantt path could differ).

rows.feature: Post a progress update after completing a milestone
rows.what: After completing a milestone in the invoice flow, the drawer offers to post an update titled “Milestone completed: {name}”.
rows.v2: Schedule › Mark done sheet › “add photos” (posted as “{milestone} is done”)
rows.how: The update rides on Done, under the studio’s update review rule.

rows.feature: Lines on a stage invoice
rows.what: The composer has a line grid (description · qty · unit · total, Enter adds a row), starting with “{milestone} (pct%)”.
rows.v2: Project › Money › stage row ⋮ › Description, note and due day
rows.how: A stage invoice is one line (its share) with an optional description; only a one-off invoice has lines of its own.

rows.feature: The total compared with the expected amount
rows.what: A banner says the total matches, is over (pick a treatment) or under (a variance and a reconcile task) the milestone’s expected amount.
rows.v2: Project › Money › stage row ⋮ › Change the amount
rows.how: The schedule’s amount sits beside the field; more than S$1 off needs a reason (“Differs from the schedule by S$x”), and the other unsent drafts take the difference in the same press.

rows.feature: Due date and a note to the client on each invoice
rows.what: The composer sets a due date (default 14 days) and “Notes (optional)”; a draft’s due date can be edited in place.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › invoice drawer · Invoices › expanded invoice › Due
rows.v2: Project › Money › row ⋮ › Description, note and due day
rows.how: Due is the payment terms (Settings › Finance › Invoices, default 7 days, 0 = on receipt), a day picked, or the project’s handover day; the note prints at the paper’s foot.

rows.feature: Pick the issuing legal entity on an invoice
rows.what: With two or more legal entities the composer offers “Issuing legal entity” (or a locked chip); the Contract/VO toolbar shows the entity tag.
rows.v2: Project › Money (the invoice’s letterhead and bank block)
rows.how: No picker: every invoice is raised under the signed quote’s issuing entity (its letterhead, bank and PayNow).

rows.feature: Fill an invoice from a PDF
rows.what: “Have a PDF? Upload PDF” reads a file with AI and pre-fills the composer’s lines, due date and notes for checking.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › invoice drawer › Compose › Upload PDF

rows.feature: Ad-hoc invoice outside the schedule
rows.what: An ad-hoc invoice with a reason chip (Material upgrade · Out-of-scope work · Reimbursement · Other), description, lines, due date and notes; it never moves the contract.
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › One-off invoice (listed under Billing › Outside the stages)

rows.feature: Turn an ad-hoc bill into a variation order
rows.what: “Capture as a Variation Order (recommended)” on the ad-hoc step opens the VO editor (nothing typed is carried over).
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Variation order
rows.how: Two separate choices in New ▾; no bridge between them.

rows.feature: Save as draft or Save & Send
rows.what: The composer saves a numbered draft or sends at once, then shows a Done card with next steps.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › invoice drawer › Compose › Done
rows.v2: Project › Money › row › Send
rows.how: Drafts already exist; Send numbers the invoice, records it and opens WhatsApp; a snackbar names the number and due day.

rows.feature: Over-bill treatments
rows.what: An over-billed invoice must pick: create a VO for the extra, front-load and rebalance, or flag it; the VO choice saves the invoice at the expected amount.
rows.how: A Draft’s amount may change with a reason; the other drafts absorb it.

rows.feature: Top-up invoice for an under-billed milestone
rows.what: A second invoice on an under-billed milestone, capped at the gap, closes its variance.

rows.feature: Reconcile tasks, variance issues and the Resolve wizard
rows.what: A non-zero variance creates a reconcile task for the designer, shows as a finance issue, and a “Resolve invoice variance” wizard records VO / rebalance / accept.
rows.v1: Overview › Financial Summary › Resolve · Project › Finance

rows.feature: The invoice list
rows.what: Invoices sub-tab: Invoice # · Description · Amount · Paid · Balance · Status · Actions, with Send / Resubmit / Record Payment on the row; cards on a phone.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing (and its Invoices view for Owners and Admins)
rows.how: Billing lists the stages as rows: Amount · Invoice (number · sent · due · how late · reminded) · Paid (receipts, credited) · Next step; voided ones as faint sub-rows; extras under “Outside the stages”.

rows.feature: Invoiced / received / outstanding figures
rows.what: A strip shows Total Invoiced (+ drafts), Total Received and Outstanding; the cockpit has “You’re owed” with overdue count.
rows.v2: Project › Money › To collect tile
rows.how: One tile: what is owed, “S$x collected of S$y” bar, the next stage; its hover lists invoiced, left to invoice, outside the contract and to confirm.

rows.feature: The opened invoice: lines, totals, payments, edit history
rows.what: Clicking a row expands it: lines, totals, Payment History, Edit History and the action buttons.
rows.v2: Project › Money › a row › the invoice panel
rows.how: A side panel with its payments (each with its own ⋮), credit notes and history (from Activity); lines and totals are on the printable page.

rows.feature: Invoice statuses
rows.what: draft · sent · partially paid · paid · overdue · void · cancelled, plus “Pending Approval” / “Approval Rejected” overlays.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing (status tag)
rows.how: Draft · Ready to send · Waiting for approval · Sent · Overdue · Part paid · Paid · Payment to confirm · Credited · Void; no Cancelled.

rows.feature: Paid and part paid worked out from payments
rows.what: An invoice’s paid amount and status are recomputed from counted payments and credits; never set by hand.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing

rows.feature: Preview an invoice as a page
rows.what: “Preview Invoice” opens a full-screen page with Back, Copy payment link and Print / PDF.
rows.v2: Project › Money › row ⋮ › Open the invoice (/projects/{id}/invoices/{invoiceId}: Download PDF · Copy the invoice link · Record a payment)

rows.feature: The invoice filed in the project’s documents
rows.what: Each invoice gets a file entry “{number}.pdf” under Financial Documents/Invoices, and a stored PDF.
rows.v2: Project › Files › Payments (“{number} · {stage}.pdf”)
rows.how: Filed on send; the entry opens the invoice’s page, printed on demand (no stored PDF).

rows.feature: Upload an invoice made outside OpenMaison
rows.what: “Upload Invoice” stores a file with reference, client, amount and date in an External Invoices card that counts in no figure (hidden until a system invoice exists).
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Record an invoice made elsewhere
rows.how: The recorded invoice counts in the figures, marked Recorded, stands for a stage or for nothing, and takes payments like any sent invoice.

rows.feature: Edit an invoice after it is made
rows.what: No screen edits lines, description or amount after saving (an editor is mounted but unreachable); the guide says invoices can be edited and deleted.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Draft row ⋮ (Change the amount · Edit the invoice · Description, note and due day · Remove the Draft)
rows.how: Drafts change; a sent invoice never does (void it and the fresh Draft takes its share).

rows.feature: Invoice approval before sending
rows.what: When the studio requires it, a non-approver’s Send leaves the invoice pending; the owner gets a task and a notice (Save & Send skipped the gate).
rows.v2: Project › Money › Submit for approval · Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Invoices need approval

rows.feature: Approve & Send
rows.what: An approver presses “Approve & Send”: the invoice is approved and sent, the client emailed and their bell rung.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you › Approve and send (also the row’s Next step)

rows.feature: Reject an invoice with a reason
rows.what: “Reject” asks what needs fixing; the invoice goes back to draft and the submitter may resubmit.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you or row ⋮ › Send back

rows.feature: Remind the approver
rows.what: “Remind approver” nudges the approver: once per member per hour and three times per invoice per day.
rows.v2: Project › Money › row ⋮ › Remind the approvers
rows.how: Once an hour per person; no daily cap of three per invoice.

rows.feature: Send an invoice to the client
rows.what: Send sets the invoice sent, queues the accounting sync and emails the client “invoice sent” with the /pay/inv link.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Send (dialog “Send via WhatsApp”)
rows.how: Send numbers it, stamps sent and due, files it and opens WhatsApp on the press with a drafted message (the portal link, or a no-login link with the bank, PayNow and reference for a client without the portal).

rows.feature: Emails to the client about invoices and receipts
rows.what: The client is emailed when an invoice is sent or approved, and when a payment’s receipt is issued (with its link).
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications (client messages) · Sent messages
rows.how: The messages are written and logged through the delivery layer; a real email / WhatsApp provider is for the developers to plug in (`setDeliveryAdapter`). The client’s portal bell rings for real.

rows.feature: Re-send an invoice already issued
rows.what: The server can re-email an issued invoice (“resend”), but no screen offers it.
rows.v2: Project › Money › row ⋮ › Remind on WhatsApp · Copy the invoice link
rows.how: Reaching the client again is the WhatsApp reminder or the copied link.

rows.feature: Void an invoice
rows.what: “Void” on a draft acts at once with no confirmation or undo; the server also allows voiding a sent invoice; a paid one cannot be voided.
rows.v2: Project › Money › sent row ⋮ › Void
rows.how: An Owner or Admin voids a sent invoice with a reason; it keeps its number, a fresh Draft takes the stage’s share, the drafts re-size, Undo. One with a payment is refused (reverse the payment first).

rows.feature: Overdue, and the studio told
rows.what: A daily job (06:00 SGT) marks sent invoices past due as overdue and notifies Owners / Admins.
rows.v2: Project › Money (Overdue) · the bell (“An invoice is overdue”) · Projects listing › Needs attention “Payment overdue”
rows.how: Worked out from the due day whenever it is read; the bell row goes to the project’s members; the client’s portal bell says it too.

rows.feature: Invoice numbers
rows.what: INV-0000 from a per-studio sequence (or the issuing entity’s prefix), given when the invoice is created; three different numbering paths existed.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Document numbers (per issuing entity too)
rows.how: INV-{YYYY}-{seq}, given only when the invoice is sent; one numbering path.

rows.feature: An invoice’s history
rows.what: Edits are logged per field with who and when and shown as “Edit History”.
rows.v2: Project › Money › invoice panel › history · Activity (Money chip)
rows.how: Made, submitted, sent back, sent, edited with its reason, reminded, paid, credited, voided — in Activity’s words.

rows.feature: The invoice the client opens without signing in
rows.what: Each invoice has a token page /pay/inv/{token}: studio letterhead, lines, totals, paid and balance, payment history, bank details, notes.
rows.v2: /invoice/{token} (Money › row ⋮ › Copy the invoice link)

rows.feature: The old single client payment link
rows.what: /pay/{token}: a phone-verified page with Overview · Invoices · Progress · Updates · Actions (approve a milestone, raise an issue); the project card that generated and revoked it is switched off, so no screen hands it out.
rows.v2: The client portal /my/{slug} (Money, Schedule, Updates…) · Project › Client access
rows.how: One signed-in portal per client replaces the token link; invoices and receipts keep their own no-login links.

rows.feature: Pay online
rows.what: The public invoice shows a disabled “Pay Online · S$x — COMING SOON”.

rows.feature: The studio’s own invoice paper
rows.what: Document templates per type (invoice · PO · VO) with an override per company: header and footer notes, terms block, acceptance terms, show / hide bank and balance, an accent colour and a live preview.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Invoice paper
rows.how: Header note, terms heading and text, footer note, show bank, show paid and balance, the studio’s and per issuing entity. No accent colour, no acceptance-terms block, no live preview. A VO prints through the quote templates.

rows.feature: “Original → adjusted” on a re-sized invoice
rows.what: After a VO moves the contract, the invoice shows the contract before and after and its own original amount next to the adjusted one.
rows.v2: The invoice paper (“Original S$x → adjusted S$y after VO-n”)

rows.feature: GST line and tax invoice wording
rows.what: The GST line prints only when the invoice carries GST, labelled with its own rate.
rows.v2: The invoice paper (“Tax invoice” when the entity is GST-registered; “GST (9%)”)

rows.feature: Log a reminder, with escalation
rows.what: “Log reminder” sends nothing: it counts reminders and, from the third, raises a high-priority escalation ticket.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Needs you or row ⋮ › Remind on WhatsApp
rows.how: The reminder opens WhatsApp with the drafted message and is counted (“reminded 2× · last 3 Oct”). No escalation is raised after repeated reminders.

rows.feature: How old each unpaid invoice is
rows.what: Rows say “{d}d overdue”, “due today”, “due in {d}d”, “sent {d}d ago”.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Overview › You’re owed drawer
rows.v2: Project › Money › Billing (Invoice cell) · Needs you rows

rows.feature: Drawers behind each figure
rows.what: Each headline figure opens a drawer: You’re owed · You owe · Invoices by stage · How profit is calculated · Cash so far.
rows.v2: Project › Money › tiles (hover = how it is made; press = its list)
rows.how: Pressing To collect goes to Billing, To pay and Profit to Costs; the lists themselves replace the drawers.

rows.feature: Record a client payment
rows.what: Amount (prefilled with the balance, Full / Half chips), method, reference, date, notes, and a list of payments so far; a full payment ends on “Payment recorded”.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Record Payment · Invoices › Record Payment
rows.v2: Project › Money › row Next step / panel / invoice page / Needs you › Record a payment
rows.how: One dialog: amount paid (what is owed, to start), paid on, how, reference, note, the bank’s confirmation (optional); confirmed on entry with its receipt; Undo for ten minutes. No Full / Half chips; earlier payments are in the invoice’s panel.

rows.feature: Mark as Paid
rows.what: “Mark as Paid” records the balance dated today with a chosen method.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Record a payment (prefilled with what is owed)
rows.how: One way to record money, not four.

rows.feature: Card and GIRO as payment methods
rows.what: Six methods: Bank Transfer · PayNow · Cheque · Cash · Credit Card · GIRO.
rows.how: Bank transfer · PayNow · Cheque · Cash remain.

rows.feature: No payment above the balance or on a draft
rows.what: The server refuses a payment on a draft, void or cancelled invoice, or above the balance.
rows.v2: Project › Money › Record a payment

rows.feature: One payment drawer for invoices and POs
rows.what: The Record Payment drawer first asks what the payment is against: a client invoice, a vendor PO, or “log it as an expense”.
rows.v2: Project › Money › each invoice’s Record a payment (vendor payments under Costs)
rows.how: The payment starts from its invoice; there is no pick step.

rows.feature: Payment verification tiers
rows.what: A payment is “ID verified” (recorded by a designer) or “management verified” (Owner / Admin / Accounting), or unverified (a client proof).
rows.v2: Project › Money (Confirmed · To confirm)
rows.how: One confirmation: what the studio records is confirmed on entry; a client’s proof waits as To confirm for the confirmer.

rows.feature: Commission accrues on each client payment
rows.what: Each client payment adds a commission accrual by the project’s / member’s / studio’s rule, split between the assignees.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Commission · Settings › Finance › Commission

notes: Read from the code of both repos; nothing was run. The Overview tab’s Financial Summary maths (C-153…C-195) are mapped here as well as in G. Unreachable 1.0 code (the invoice editor, Generate Invoices, Record Delivery, the Collected drawer, the Client Portal link card, vendor VOs) and 1.0’s own faults are folded into the rows they belong to rather than listed. Money out (POs, bills, expenses, vendors) and the studio-wide Finance pages, reports, commission and Xero are only touched where a money-in step reaches them. One rule worth a look: an approved, client-confirmed VO can be deleted from the quote editor and leaves the contract silently (MI-104). Xero’s “Push automatically” is wired to credit-note and commission steps only, not to sending an invoice or recording a payment.
